notes.source_text: Both groups complete one paper diary entry each evening from the day after randomization (Day 1) through Day 56 inclusive, about two minutes per day. Each entry records total screen-use hours and whether screen use occurred. Scheduled-break participants additionally record the number of eligible 30-minute intervals and the number followed by a completed two-minute break. Usual-habits participants record the number of breaks they naturally took; they are not given adherence targets. An evening entry is not a clinic visit. Day 0 has no home-diary entry. Clinic visits are not multiplied by diary days. Do not invent daily symptom ratings: the diary does not collect symptom scores.
notes.display_text: Home activity, separate from clinic visits: both groups complete one paper-diary entry each evening on Days 1–56 inclusive, beginning the day after randomization, for about two minutes daily. Usual-habits participants record naturally taken breaks without adherence targets. There is no Day 0 home entry, and the diary collects no symptom scores.

Mix-and-match implantation of PureSee in the dominant eye and Odyssey in the non-dominant eye may provide a broader range of vision and fewer visual disturbances than bilateral implantation of either lens alone. Excellent distance, intermediate and near vision, high satisfaction and fewer visual disturbances remain hypothesized rather than established benefits. Participants may receive no direct benefit; findings may improve understanding of outcomes with this combination.

Using PureSee in your dominant eye and Odyssey in your other eye may give you a wider range of vision and fewer unwanted visual effects than using the same lens in both eyes. benefit_interpretation.rationale: The combination has a source-supported possible benefit, not an established advantage. The paragraph preserves the lens-to-eye relationship, comparison and uncertainty without treating earlier individual-lens studies as proof of benefit.

Mix-and-match implantation of PureSee in the dominant eye and Odyssey in the non-dominant eye may provide a broader range of vision and fewer visual disturbances than bilateral implantation of either lens alone. Excellent distance, intermediate and near vision, high satisfaction and fewer visual disturbances remain hypothesized rather than established benefits. Participants may receive no direct benefit; findings may improve understanding of outcomes with this combination.

Using PureSee in your dominant eye and Odyssey in your other eye may give you a wider range of vision and fewer unwanted visual effects than using the same lens in both eyes. Clear vision at different distances, less need for glasses and greater satisfaction are possible benefits, not proven results or promises. You may receive no direct benefit. The study may help researchers better understand outcomes with this combination.
